transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So this is the mouth that fell after the hand took its prize. You smell of bravado scraped thin by the drop. Speak—quickly, or carefully—those are your first choices.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Shut up and get out of my way! I don't care about your riddles or who you are, just give me my brother back!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Shut up'—that is a broom-word, used when you have nothing shaped to offer. 'Get out of my way' tells me you think this place is a corridor, not a throat. You say 'brother' last, like an afterthought; say it again, or say more, and choose which word you mean.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He's not an afterthought, he's the only reason I'm down in this pit! Stop analyzing me and move your giant self aside!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Pit' is a small word for a place that eats names; it tells me you are still pretending height matters here. 'Giant' is just fear trying to look insulting, and 'move aside' assumes I am furniture. You say he is the only reason—then use his name, or explain why you keep him faceless.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: His name is Omar, and I'm sick of your stupid riddles! Just get out of my face and let me in!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Stupid' is a lazy stone; you throw it when your hands shake. 'Get out of my face' tells me you think I am blocking your eyes, not your courage. You finally gave him a name—Omar—so say what you did when the well answered him instead of you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared him to insult the well! It's my fault, okay, so stop staring and get out of my way!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Dared' is a child's crown; it sits lightly and falls at the first scream. 'My fault' you say quickly, like tossing a coin to pay a debt you have not counted. And 'stop staring'—there is no stare here, only attention, and it has just begun; continue.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You're just a door guard. You don't decide anything down here. I'm walking past you whether you like it or not.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A door guard is exactly what stands between you and what you want, which makes me the only thing that matters to you right now. You are trying to shrink me so you feel taller. Say what you think waits for Omar, or keep wasting breath.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll find another way in if I have to tear this gate off myself. You're not going to talk me to death down here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Tear it off'—you picture force as a key because thinking feels too slow. 'Talk me to death' tells me you are afraid of what you might say if you slow down. Say what you plan to do when you find him and he does not recognize your face.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll hold him with my bare hands, just shut up and get out of the way! I'm sick of listening to you, so move!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Bare hands'—you offer skin as if it were a tool, as if grip were stronger than memory. 'Shut up' returns again, thin and shiny from overuse; you keep polishing that word instead of sharpening another. You say you're sick of listening, yet you keep talking—what are you afraid I'll hear if you stop?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You think you scare me? I've seen scarier things in my village. You're just a big ugly statue blocking a door.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A statue does not speak, and you are still here, answering me. You came to a place that eats names and you call it ordinary—that is not bravery, that is noise you use to cover the shaking. Say what Omar's voice sounded like before the well took him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He didn't become anything, you stupid monster, he's just a scared kid! Stop talking trash and move your big ugly self aside!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Monster' is a mask-word; you put it on me so you don't have to look at what pulls below. 'Just a scared kid'—that is the first clean thing you've said, and you rush past it like it burns. You call my words trash, yet you keep throwing yours at the gate; say what scared Omar said before the well took him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: None of this is any of your business! You don't know anything about me or Omar, so stop pretending you do!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Everything that crosses this threshold is my business. You walked in carrying his name and your guilt and you want me to look away from both. I know what you brought down here—say what you told him to scream, or admit you don't want to hear it again.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't owe you anything! Not my words, not my reasons, nothing. Just get out of my face.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You owe me nothing, and yet you are still standing here. You could have turned back at the drop, at the dark, at my face—but you kept moving. Something in you owes something to him; say what it is, or keep throwing empty hands.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not playing your stupid games, you ugly giant! Just shut your mouth and get out of my way!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Games'—you keep using that word for any path where you might have to choose; I hear only evasion. 'Ugly giant' again, circling the same shallow pool because it's safer than depth. You are not angry at me; you are afraid that if you stop shouting, Omar's voice will be louder than yours—say whether you miss it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I miss him, okay? I miss him, you stupid giant, so shut your mouth and move!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Stupid'—you reach for it the moment something true slips out, as if the word could shove it back in. 'I miss him' is heavy, and you slap it with an insult to see if it will break and stop hurting. Say more than that, or keep choosing noise over him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need him back more than air, you heartless monster! Just shut your mouth and let me through!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Heartless'—you say it because you are drowning and want someone else to lack breath instead of you. 'More than air' is the truth stretching its neck, and you try to strangle it with 'monster.' If you need him that much, tell me what you would give up that you're still clinging to.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'd give up my own life, you stupid, ugly giant! Just shut your mouth and let me pass!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Give up my life'—you throw it like a coin you've never tried to spend, bright and untested. 'Stupid, ugly giant' follows fast, because saying that costs you nothing and keeps the harder price safely unnamed. You didn't come to die; you came because you told Omar to speak—tell me what you hoped would happen when he did.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I thought it was just a joke, you brainless idiot! I didn't know a freak like you was actually listening!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Brainless'—you choose it because thinking is exactly what you are avoiding. 'Joke' is the word humans use when they want to rinse blood off their hands without water. You didn't know I was listening, but you knew something was, and you fed it your brother—say what you felt when the hand came out.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I froze like a coward, you stupid pile of dirt! I couldn't do anything, so shut your mouth and let me through!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You named yourself just now—coward—and buried it fast under the insult. Freezing is not nothing; it is the body choosing to live while the soul watches and remembers. Tell me what Omar's face did when you didn't move.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He looked at me like I betrayed him, you ugly freak! Just shut your mouth and let me pass!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Ugly freak' again—when the word 'betrayed' gets too close, you shove it at my shape and hope it sticks there instead of on you. 'Betrayed' is the truest word you have brought, and you rushed past it like it was burning your tongue. Say what his face looked like when you didn't move.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm sorry I was too scared to save you, Omar, I'm sorry I'm a coward! Now move your ugly, giant face and let me tell him that!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You spent 'sorry' like a stone thrown past him, already turning back to hit me with 'ugly' so you wouldn't have to stay with it. You wanted the gate to carry your words so you wouldn't have to, and you wasted the moment by aiming them at my face instead of his silence. That is what you chose to spend your breath on.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Don't you dare say I'm done, you stupid, heartless liar! I have to tell him I love him, so get out of my way!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Liar'—because if I were lying, then the moment wouldn't be gone. You had 'I love him' circling your mouth since you arrived and you kept swallowing it to throw an insult instead. I am not the one keeping it from him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then stop blocking me, you giant, ugly freak! I just want to say it to his face!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'Say it to his face'—and yet you have not managed to say it once without something sharp attached. You had thirty chances to put it down clean and you spent every one adding a blade. That is not my doing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm saying it now! I love him, okay? I love him, so just move!

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: 'So just move'—even now, even here, you cannot let it land without a shove behind it. You said the true thing and then immediately used it as a lever. The gate does not open for love with handles on it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know how to say it without the anger. I don't know how.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I know. And it is too late to learn it here. Go back up. Come back when you know what to do with your mouth when the thing you love is listening.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can't go back without him.
